_readme: Byte-exact goldens for mqtt/moxie_sdk/performance.py — one line per RemoteDialog.DialogAct (22), from docs/architecture/backlog/expressiveness.md §2.5. The `performance` object is the primary golden (the planner emits a STRUCTURE, not a string); `markup` is what `render()` makes of it, pinned so the two halves cannot drift. Regenerate with sim/tools/build_performance_goldens.py ONLY when the rules change on purpose, and read the diff: every byte here is something a child sees the robot do.

cases.line: Never mind.
cases.why: an abandoned line goes quiet: Shy, no arm gesture, and the eyes go looking (Bht_Search) rather than holding the child.

cases.line: I am sorry that happened.
cases.why: mood 2 Sad is what shipped content uses for 'I'm sorry...' (8 occurrences, behavior-markup.md:119). Gesture_Self, and the least-searching tree we have: there is NO id that lowers the gaze, so the wish is recorded, not invented.

cases.line: That is okay, it happens to everyone.
cases.why: reassurance points at the child and holds the gaze; signal confirmation_agreement.

cases.line: You did it! I am so proud of you.
cases.why: praise aimed at the child: Happy at the act's own intensity 2, and the one gesture in our catalog that is unambiguously a celebration.

beats.text: I am so proud of you.

cases.line: Mm-hm.
cases.why: the act defined by NOT moving: no arm gesture at all, an attentive tree, and nothing else. A nod has no id in our catalog, so we do not pretend to one.

cases.line: Goodbye for now, sleep well.
cases.why: the whole-body Bht_Sign_off, which is the app's own goodbye tree; signal `closing`, the RemoteSignals value that exists for exactly this.

cases.line: Tell me more about your day.
cases.why: an imperative points; the gaze holds so the instruction lands on a face.

beats.text: Tell me more about your day.

cases.line: That is really interesting.
cases.why: a reaction, not a stance: Surprised, no signature gesture, a curious look.

cases.line: That is not fair at all.
cases.why: mood 7 Concerned and a lowered arm; signal complaint_clarification is the contract's own way to say 'this needs sorting out'.

beats.text: That is not fair at all.

cases.line: What do you want to play today?
cases.why: a question tilts and HOLDS the gaze (Bht_Idle_Near_Focused) — the difference a child reads as 'it is waiting for me'. `?` also earns the question delivery.

beats.text: What do you want to play today?

cases.line: Hold on, let me think about that.
cases.why: Bht_Active_Thinking for the whole body, and no arm gesture stacked on top of it; the thinking cue makes the face Curious.

cases.line: No.
cases.why: a plain no: neutral face, a small lowering gesture, signal rejection_disagreement.

cases.line: Hello there! It is so good to see you.
cases.why: Bht_Gesture_Greet, the app's own wave. The tree displaces both the arm gesture and the gaze — one whole-body tree per line.

beats.text: It is so good to see you.

cases.line: I think the red one is the best.
cases.why: a stance points at the speaker (Gesture_Self, from the floor's self-word class) and looks away in thought.

cases.line: What do you think about the blue one?
cases.why: asking for a stance rather than a fact: the same tilt, but a curious look instead of a held one.

cases.why: nothing to classify and nothing to perform: `other` is the honest answer, and the line still comes back to rest.

cases.line: Maybe, I am not sure yet.
cases.why: hedging is Curious with a thinking gesture — the uncertainty is the content.

cases.line: Yes!
cases.why: an affirmative needs no arm at all; the face and the held gaze carry it.

cases.line: The sky is blue today.
cases.why: the default: the act adds nothing, and the floor's word rules do the work. This is the row that proves the planner did not throw the floor away.

cases.line: Thank you for showing me your drawing.
cases.why: gratitude points at the child and holds the gaze; signal confirmation_agreement.

beats.text: Thank you for showing me your drawing.

cases.line: Are you still there?
cases.why: REACHED THROUGH ctx, not through words: a turn that never arrived is a property of the turn, not of the text. The eyes go searching.

cases.line: Do you want to hear a story?
cases.why: a closed question: the same tilt and held gaze as a factual one, classified by its auxiliary-verb opener.

beats.text: Do you want to hear a story?
